key_points: A function assigns exactly one output to each input. The domain is the set of allowed inputs and the range is the set of outputs (Lecture1.pdf p.10).
Find the domain by excluding values that make a denominator zero or a radicand negative (Lecture1.pdf p.12).
A function is increasing on I if x < x' implies f(x) < f(x'), and decreasing if x < x' implies f(x) > f(x') (Lecture1.pdf p.20).
f is even if f(-x) = f(x), with y-axis symmetry. f is odd if f(-x) = -f(x), with origin symmetry (Lecture1.pdf p.22-23).
For an even or odd function, sketching x >= 0 is enough, because the rest of the graph follows from symmetry (Lecture1.pdf p.24).
guide.explanation: A function is a rule that gives exactly one output for each input, and its domain and range describe the allowed inputs and resulting outputs. Monotonicity is read from whether f(x) rises or falls as x increases on an interval. Even and odd symmetry come from comparing f(-x) with f(x) and -f(x).
guide.example: Check whether f(x) = x^3 - x is even, odd, or neither. Compute f(-x) = (-x)^3 - (-x) = -x^3 + x = -(x^3 - x) = -f(x). Since f(-x) = -f(x) for all x, f is odd, so its graph is symmetric about the origin (Lecture1.pdf p.23).

questions.question: What is the domain of f(x) = 1/(x - 1)?
options: All real x greater than or equal to 1
questions.explanation: The denominator x - 1 is zero only when x = 1, so the domain is {x != 1} (Lecture1.pdf p.12).

questions.question: Which symmetry does f(x) = x^2 have?
questions.explanation: (-x)^2 = x^2 = f(x) for all x, so f is even and symmetric about the y-axis (Lecture1.pdf p.22).

questions.question: Show that f(x) = x^3 is odd by checking the defining condition.
questions.answer: f(-x) = (-x)^3 = -x^3 = -f(x) for all x, so f is odd.
questions.explanation: An odd function satisfies f(-x) = -f(x) wherever it is defined. The cube of -x is -x^3, which matches this condition (Lecture1.pdf p.23).

questions.question: The function on Lecture1.pdf p.21 is decreasing on [0,1] and [4.2,5] and increasing on [1,4.2]. On which interval is it increasing?
questions.explanation: The text states the function is increasing on [1,4.2] and decreasing on the other two intervals (Lecture1.pdf p.21).

questions.question: What is the domain of g(x) = sqrt(x - 2), using real numbers?
questions.answer: x >= 2, written as {x in R : x >= 2}
questions.explanation: The square root is real only when x - 2 >= 0, so x >= 2. Lecture1.pdf p.12 gives this same domain for the second exercise.

questions.question: What does the vertical line test check?
options: Whether each x has at most one output y, so the curve is a function
Whether the function is continuous at every point
Whether the slope of the graph is constant
questions.answer: Whether each x has at most one output y, so the curve is a function
questions.explanation: A curve is not the graph of a function if a vertical line meets it at two or more points, because one x would have two y-values (Lecture1.pdf p.16).

questions.question: Why does knowing that a function is even or odd save work when sketching its graph?
questions.answer: You only need to sketch the part for x >= 0, then use symmetry to get the rest: reflection across the y-axis for even functions and across the origin for odd functions.
questions.explanation: Symmetry means the other half of the graph is determined by the positive-x half, which halves the sketching work (Lecture1.pdf p.22-24).
